title: Holomorphic compactly supported regularizing perturbations of Green-hyperbolic operators with discrete exceptional parameters
author: Christopher J. Fewster
source_version: Official SIGMA 19 (2023) article 057, DOI 10.3842/SIGMA.2023.057; journal PDF and native TeX acquired 2026-09-30, exact bytes pinned by SHA256
difficulty_reason: The proof synchronizes analytic Fredholm inverses across every Sobolev order and upgrades them to the bounded-convergence topology of smooth compactly supported functions. It extends the compact-support inverse to the LF test-function space, constructs both Green operators and proves the precise causal support alternative. A separate holomorphic support argument recovers ordinary Green propagation for support-nonincreasing modifications, so this is more than applying the analytic Fredholm theorem at one Hilbert-space level.

source_check.note: The complete Theorem3.1, Theorem5.1, Corollary5.2, Lemma5.3 and the technical bounded-convergence support lemmas A.2–A.6 are supplied. The standing manifold is a globally hyperbolic spacetime with finitely many connected components and fixed topologically regular compact K; P acts on smooth scalar functions. A(0)=0, range A(lambda) is supported in K, the stated distribution/Sobolev extensions improve total regularity by delta=beta+gamma>0, and A(lambda)E+/- is holomorphic at all relevant Sobolev levels. The full source assumptions (a)–(d) and the stronger (d-prime) alternative are retained literally, without reducing them to the misleading shorthand smoothing perturbation. Established Green-hyperbolic extension theory and analytic Fredholm theory are background; the new smooth/LF inversion, Green identities, parameter continuity and support construction are fully proved here. The dual-kernel comparison3.5 and special integral-kernel corollaries are not counted separately. Source approval supplied only by exact frozen root input; no new source/difficulty decision or mathematical referee.
